A1.justification: Both PDFs describe ConlangCrafter. The complete main texts, figures, tables, equations, and appendices A–D support reliable comparison, including matching material relocated between versions.

before.justification: V3 reports original conlang-generation experiments, baseline comparisons, component and temperature ablations, and manual expert evaluation.

after.justification: V4 retains these original empirical results and adds analyses of typological feature coverage and similarity to natural languages.

M1.justification: The staged generation pipeline, randomness injection, self-refinement, constructive translation, and appendix prompts are unchanged. V4's clarification that evaluation excludes sketch updates was already documented in v3 Appendix A.4.

E1.justification: Both versions use the same conlang-generation tasks, ten translation sentences, WALS data, and user-controlled scenarios. The all-vowel and cephalopod examples in v4 Table 4 were already present in v3 Table 6; the nearest-neighbor analysis uses the existing WALS source.

E2.justification: Tables 1–3 retain the same single-stage baseline, component variants, and temperature-sampling comparisons. Newly cited works do not introduce evaluated comparison methods.

E3.justification: Appendix A.6 replaces the stated range of 17–21 generated languages with 16 for Gemini-2.5-Flash, 20 for Gemini-2.5-Pro, and 24 for DeepSeek-R1. This is a reported setting revision, without evidence establishing reruns. Section 3.3 also introduces a nearest-neighbor evaluation procedure using Hamming distance against WALS.

E4.justification: V4 adds a focused nearest-natural-language analysis to assess typological novelty and reports feature coverage to address underspecification. The component ablations, temperature analysis, and qualitative generation cases already existed in v3.

E5.justification: Standard errors, two-sided t-tests, Cohen's d, and manual-agreement statistics were already reported in v3 and retain the same reporting practices. The new nearest-neighbor mean and range are descriptive results, not additional uncertainty estimation.

E6.justification: V4 newly reports 94–98% feature coverage and Gemini-2.5-Pro nearest-language matches averaging 56.4%, ranging from 50.0% to 68.8%. Appendix C adds Gemini-2.5-Flash usage of approximately 2.15M tokens per language with translations. Tables 1–3 and manual-agreement results retain all displayed values.

T1.justification: The diversity and consistency definitions remain unchanged. Neither version supplies theoretical proofs, and the added nearest-neighbor analysis applies existing Hamming distance without introducing new formal assumptions or derivations.

C1.justification: The abstract, three research questions, and central contributions retain their meaning: computational conlanging through a modular pipeline and scalable evaluation. The expanded conclusion emphasizes existing applications and speculative extensions without redefining the core contribution.

C2.justification: V4 explicitly acknowledges annotator priming, the unresolved quantitative evaluation of user-constraint adherence, and biases potentially missed by its metrics. It also adds arguments contextualizing moderate annotator agreement and interpreting high feature coverage as limiting missingness effects.

D1.justification: Appendices A.5–A.6 newly disclose default scikit-learn t-SNE settings and approximately 5–10% rejection of malformed outputs. Appendix C adds Gemini-2.5-Flash token usage and identifies major cost sources. Project access information and the full prompts are retained.

R1.justification: V4 adds Schreyer (2021), Amidei et al. (2018), Van der Lee et al. (2021), Chen et al. (2024), and Singh et al. (2025), supporting conlang background, human-evaluation interpretation, and multilingual-bias limitations. The substantive positioning in Section 4 remains unchanged.

P1.justification: V4 edits introductory language, adds descriptive subheadings within results, expands evaluation explanations and the conclusion, and reorganizes limitations into paragraphs. The overall section structure and most existing prose remain intact.

P2.justification: Table 4 incorporates two existing Table 6 examples under a new divider and revised caption; Table 6 correspondingly shrinks. Figure 3 changes columns, other tables reflow, and page numbers appear. The figures themselves and appendix prompt displays are retained.

improvement.justification: V4 adds targeted evidence for typological novelty, explicitly acknowledges annotation priming, and improves technical and resource reporting. These changes modestly improve support and transparency around retained methods and performance tables. The sample-count revision remains unexplained as a correction versus rerunning experiments, limiting the gain in experimental clarity.
